messages.author: 53af45eda385f463
messages.subject: Shiny Server with proxy
parts:
On the RStudio Server documentation page, they recommend running RStudio through an Apache/Nginx proxy.  It sounds like the same approach would be useful for Shiny Server setups.  I'm new to Linux/server stuff, so does anyone know if the step-by-step instructions for setting up Shiny Server with a proxy would be the same?  Presumably, I'll have to change localhost:8787 to localhost:3838, but would everything else be the same?

Thanks for your help,
Ben

OK - I have the proxy set up, and it is successfully passing to shiny-server.

Now how do I turn off the ability to access shiny-server through port 3838?  This is the equivalent of the
www-address=127.0.0.1
command in the RStudio setup, but I can't figure out what the analogous command for shiny-server is and where I should put it.

My best guess is in the /usr/local/lib/node_modules/shiny-server/config/default.config file, but that's just a guess.

Thanks again,
Ben

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server with proxy
parts:
Copy /usr/local/lib/node_modules/shiny-server/config/default.config to /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf

Then edit the latter, where it says "listen 3838;" change it to "listen 3838 127.0.0.1;"

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server with proxy
parts:
Hi Ken, RStudio Server is a different piece of software than Shiny Server. The former is used to interactively work with an R session as is you're running RStudio on your desktop; one of the features is that you (as an RStudio user) can run Shiny apps as if from your own desktop. The latter is used to make your Shiny app generally available to anyone with a web browser.

See:
https://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/download-server/
http://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#quick-start
